name: Firebase Authentication

dataTypes.when: Whenever a user signs in (including anonymous sign-in): Firebase Auth generates and stores a unique Firebase Authentication user ID.
Only if the app uses email/password, email-link, or a federated provider whose response contains an email address.
Only if the app uses phone authentication, phone number as a sign-in method, or SMS as a second factor.
Only if the developer sets a display name, or a federated provider supplies one.

ask: Which sign-in methods do you enable (anonymous, email/password, email link, phone, Google, Facebook, Apple, etc.)? Remove Email address / Phone number entries that do not apply.

Do you use third-party providers (Facebook, Twitter, GitHub...)? Firebase collects contact information from those providers depending on granted scopes; check that provider's own disclosure and any extra data (e.g. profile photo).
Do you use phone auth? It also uses Play Integrity / reCAPTCHA Enterprise tokens; review those SDKs' disclosures.
Do you offer in-app account deletion? Play requires a deletion path for apps that let users create accounts.

sources.title: Prepare for Google Play's data disclosure requirements (Firebase)

notes: Firebase also lists automatic collection of the IP address 'to provide added security and prevent abuse during sign-up and authentication', user-agent strings, the Firebase Android App ID and the Firebase user agent. Play has no IP-address data type and this IP use is not location; it is not mapped here, but reviewers may choose to add the 'Fraud prevention, security, and compliance' purpose. Purpose source: Firebase says the data is used 'to enable authentication and account management'. Firebase's page does not give a per-product collected/shared table; it states globally that Firebase does not transfer the listed data to third parties except to subprocessors that help provide Firebase services or per the developer's instructions (e.g. linking to non-Firebase services). On that basis shared=false and role=service-provider. The page lists raw data items (e.g. 'stack traces', 'IP address'), not Play data-type labels; the mapping to Play labels and purposes here is ours.
